meta.title: Ch 10: Review of Financial Information — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 10 (Review of Financial Information).

questions.q: A review of financial information (SRE framework) concludes with:
o: A negative conclusion: nothing has come to the practitioner's attention indicating material modification
questions.why: Limited assurance = 'nothing has come to our attention' phrasing, obtained via inquiries and analytical procedures and less evidence; it is NEITHER an audit NOR an attestation of accuracy — a weaker ladder rung, honestly labelled.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — negative assurance is the review's signature phrase Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: A review is a smoke test, not a fire audit.

questions.q: The difference between SRE 2410 (review of interim by the entity's auditor) and SRE 2400 (by a practitioner not associated with the entity) includes:
o: 2400 applies to a party not connected with the entity; 2410 leverages existing knowledge while keeping independence and objectivity
questions.why: 2410 uses the auditor's own knowledge of the entity (efficiency) and applies audit-style expectations; 2400 is the 'external reviewer' standard for a non-associated practitioner — both limited assurance, different scopes and sources of familiarity.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — same ladder, different climber AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A familiar auditor and a stranger both read smoke with different eyes.

questions.q: In an interim review, the practitioner performs:
o: Physical verification of inventory at all sites
Inquiries (including of those with financial responsibility) and analytical procedures, reading the statements for consistency with other knowledge
questions.why: The review toolkit is inquiry + analytics (+ reading, comparison with prior periods, discussions with board/audit committee) — no substantive tests of details unless anomalies arise; knowing that answers half the 'not enough work' complaints.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — inquiries and analytics — substantive only on red flag Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A review is a thermometer, not an MRI.

questions.q: A review engagement is designed to:
o: Provide limited assurance that nothing indicates material modification — not to detect fraud or errors
questions.why: The purpose paragraph: reviews are not audits; fraud detection isn't designed-in (but findings still must be addressed).
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — read the level of the ladder AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A smoke alarm is not a fire department.

questions.q: Half-yearly/quarterly review obligations of the statutory auditor for listed entities run via:
o: A review-level engagement under the review standards (negative assurance, inquiry+analytics) reported in the prescribed format to the exchange/board
questions.why: The listing-regulation overlay turns the SA review framework into a compliance routine — the practical answer: same level (limited), stricter calendar, and the auditor's review procedures feed the annual audit's expectations too.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the calendar changed, the assurance didn't AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: Interim financial information of listed entities is subjected to a REVIEW rather than an audit because:
o: Listing obligations require timely, limited-assurance scrutiny of each quarter's numbers; an audit quarterly would be impractical
questions.why: The trade-off is speed versus depth: quarterly reporting demands quick turnaround, so SEBI-listed obligations pair it with review-level (limited) assurance under SRE — negative assurance wording — while annual numbers carry the reasonable-assurance audit.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — quarterly speed buys negative assurance; annual weight buys the opinion AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Twelve glimpses beat one autopsy for keeping the patient alive.

questions.q: Planning materiality for an interim review is set:
o: Identically to the audit's annual materiality
Against interim financial information — a smaller base (e.g., annualised interim profit) needs professional judgment because interim results are more volatile
questions.why: Interim statements are partial-period; a percentage of annualised figures, with sensitivity to seasonality and volatility, is the documented practice — the framework sets no bright line, so the reasoning matters more than the number in the answer.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the base shrinks, the judgment grows Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

questions.q: During a review, the practitioner is unable to read the latest board minutes. Proper response:
o: Ask for them; if unavailable for material matters, evaluate as a limitation: consider the impact on the conclusion and, where pervasive, resign/report
Include in the report? not required
Extend the review to an audit
questions.why: Review ≠ 'no procedures': its defined procedures include reading minutes; refusal/inaccessibility narrows what the conclusion can honestly say — negative assurance cannot survive a deliberate hole.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — a review's floor is still a floor Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A review with locked doors reads no assurance.

questions.q: A review's inquiry should include related-party transactions because:
o: The RPT area is where year-end manipulation concentrates — inquiries about new/undisclosed RPTs are expected, and findings escalate targeted work
questions.why: Limited assurance still requires asking the right questions: RPTs and new arrangements are named review topics — a 'no concerns' answer is only as strong as its corroboration where the prior audit found issues.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the short ladder still has rungs named AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Reviews miss plenty; RPTs aren't an excuse to.
